result:
At the edge of the harbor, a lighthouse kept shining long after the last boat had come in.

It didn’t know who might need it. Maybe a sailor lost in fog. Maybe someone walking home along the seawall, wanting proof that the dark had an edge. Maybe nobody at all.

Still, every few seconds, it turned its bright eye over the water.

The lighthouse had learned that usefulness and certainty were different things. You could do your small task without knowing whether it mattered. You could leave a light on without knowing who would see it.

And sometimes, on a very clear night, the beam crossed the waves and found another light answering from far away.
